text:
Dawson Mercer spent 410 games in New Jersey before the trade to Winnipeg, and a dozen games in, the move is starting to look comfortable. He has eight points, five of them goals, in his last ten, including a first-star night against his old team and two goals in an 8-3 win over Dallas.

Our numbers say to enjoy it without leaning on it. His own chances in that stretch, 2.2 expected goals, are exactly his usual rate, so the hot streak is mostly bounces. What looks real is the fit. The Jets take a slightly bigger share of shot attempts and chances with him on the ice than without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why linemates like him: he's often on the receiving end of passes across the slot, the shots that went in 25% of the time last season against 6% for a shooter making his own play.

At 25, with 103 career goals, he's a middle-six forward who can move up the lineup. Our projection lands him around 42 points, right where his New Jersey years would suggest.
headline: Mercer is settling in, with some help from luck
